newsitem.title: USA: NHL expansion committee chooses four cities-report.
newsitem.headline: NHL expansion committee chooses four cities-report.

text.p: The National Hockey League's expansion committee is expected to recommend Tuesday that the league accept franchise bids from groups in Atlanta, Nashville, St. Paul and Columbus, Ohio, according to media reports.
A Nashville franchise would join the league in 1998, followed by Atlanta in 1999 and St. Paul and Columbus in 2000, according to reports from Toronto-based Sports Network, CNN/SI and USA Today.
The expansion committee recommendations would then go before the NHL's ruling board of governors for approval at its June 25 meeting.
An NHL spokesman would not confirm the reports, but noted that expansion would likely be on the agenda for the June 25 meeting.
The expansion committee also considered bids from Houston and Oklahoma City groups. Each ownership group must pay an $80 million franchise fee.
Nashville already has an arena ready for a new franchise. Atlanta, St. Paul and Columbus all recently completed financing plans for new arenas that would include at least some issuance of bonds.
A $213 million Atlanta arena would rely in part on $140 million of revenue bonds.

St. Paul has committed to $30 million of bonds for a new $130 million arena and pledged to issue another $65 million of debt if Minnesota lawmakers choose not to include it in a capital spending bill next year.
Columbus has approved private financing for a $125 million arena that would include more than $20 million of infrastructure improvements paid by the city and Franklin County.
